bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Occupational health and safety across long-haul transport, warehousing and hazardous-cargo handling — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications. Given operations in long-distance transportation, warehousing, cargo handling and movement of diverse consignments including hazardous and chemical goods, road accidents, driver fatigue, workplace incidents and health-related risks may adversely impact employees, business continuity, operational efficiency and stakeholder confidence. Mitigation is an EHS framework with PPE, driver and employee safety training, stringent cargo-handling protocols, 24x7 GPS-enabled fleet monitoring through centralised control towers, medical/insurance cover and the TCI Safe Safar driver initiative.
- Talent attraction, development and retention — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: inability to attract, develop and retain skilled talent may impact operational efficiency, service quality, productivity and the Company's ability to meet customer expectations and growth objectives. Mitigated through structured learning and development, job rotation, upskilling/reskilling, leadership development, performance-based progression, recognition programmes, ESOPs and academic/industry partnerships for a talent pipeline.
- Cyber security and IT resilience — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications — worldwide businesses have reported newer and emerging cybersecurity threats such as ransomware, posing risk to everyday business operations. The Company states it has adequate cyber and IT security systems including ITDR, verified by external consultants with all recommendations implemented. Exposure is structurally rising as operations become dependent on proprietary TMS/WMS, control towers and digital documentation.
- Climate change and extreme weather disruption — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk: climate change can impact operations through extreme weather events such as cyclones, heat waves and floods, which have the potential to create severe disruptions to a pan-India road, rail and coastal network (the mitigation text is truncated in the routed source).
- Geopolitical disruption to trade lanes, energy and freight costs — The MD&A records that the US-Israel and Iran conflict, escalating since February 2026, has hit critical maritime choke points including the Strait of Hormuz, forcing vessel rerouting, suspended operations and a surge in war-risk surcharges and insurance premiums; Gulf airspace closures cut global air cargo capacity by approximately 18%; and energy-market volatility spiked bunker fuel prices, creating cascading cost pressure across supply chains. Coastal shipping and cross-border operations sit directly in this exposure.
- Structural dependence on a contract/outsourced workforce — The BRSR workforce table shows Nil permanent workers against 8,904 workers who are 'other than permanent', alongside 4,165 permanent employees. Service quality, safety compliance and cost are therefore delivered largely through a non-permanent workforce and vendor/driver ecosystem the Company does not employ directly.
- Domestic and single-geography concentration — Exports contribute only 0.18% of total turnover and international presence is limited to three countries (Bangladesh, Nepal, UAE) with no international offices reported in the BRSR operations table, so earnings are tied almost entirely to Indian freight, warehousing and coastal demand cycles despite the Company's stated global-connectivity ambition.
- Competitive/technology displacement as digitalisation becomes the baseline — The MD&A states that logistics digitalisation has shifted from a competitive advantage to a fundamental operational requirement and that organisations failing to embed technology into core workflows now operate at a structural disadvantage, with ~70% of logistics enterprises accelerating digital transformation — implying continuous, non-discretionary technology spend simply to hold position.
- Customer service-quality and grievance exposure — The BRSR transparency table reports 3,238 customer complaints filed in FY 2025-26 (figures reworked to include all major and material complaints), handled through a toll-free number, email and an escalation matrix — a scale-driven service-quality watch item in a business whose differentiation is stated to be reliability and visibility.

business.body:
- Branded "Everything Logistics"; FY 2025-26 integrated strengths cited as 7 decades of industry leadership, 10,000+ trucks in operation, 67 yards managed, 17 Mn sq.ft. managed warehouse space, 1,400+ IT-enabled own offices and 2.0% of India's GDP moved by value.
- Strategy rests on four planks: creating value in high-growth industry sectors, a wide range of bespoke solutions for diverse industries, strong multimodal capabilities and network, and technology/automation-driven operations, delivered under a single window.
- Present across eleven industry verticals, named ones including Automotive & Mobility (JV with Mitsui - Transystem), Consumption-Led Sectors, Hi-Tech & Electronics, Metals & Construction, Energy & Renewables and Chemicals & Pharma (TCI Chemlog, cold chain, AEO-certified customs).
- Market framing by segment: Freight in a "USD 180 Bn Freight Transport Market - highly fragmented and unorganized" with LTL "relatively organized, with 15% share"; Supply Chain in a "USD 15 Bn" market where 3PL penetration is 4.5% in India vs 11% globally.
- Digital moat framed as a three-layer architecture: Visibility (3 division Control Towers for Freight, SCS, Seaways with live GPS tracking, ETA variance and exception alerts), Intelligence (MILKRUN route consolidation, Delivery Optimisation Engine, CNS AI document-intelligence layer) and Integration (single shipment identity across road, rail and sea, with emissions measured end-to-end through TEMT).

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: TCI operates a comprehensive multimodal logistics portfolio built around three main activities: Freight Transport (organised surface transport covering FTL, LTL, over-dimensional cargo and project heavy haul across India and SAARC/BBIN nations), Supply Chain Solutions (a single-window enabler covering network design, inventory management, modern warehousing and multimodal transportation from 'conceptualization to implementation'), and Coastal Transportation (multimodal coastal shipping connecting India's western, eastern and southern ports with first- and last-mile rail and road connectivity). Execution is supported by an asset-backed network — vehicles, warehousing, yards, hubs and branches — and a digital backbone of proprietary Transportation and Warehouse Management Systems, control towers and AI/ML-driven route and network optimisation. Customers span automotive, chemicals, engineering, retail, e-commerce, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, FMCG, consumer durables and defence.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Evolve from a transporter into an integrated logistics orchestration platform — "Everything Logistics" — combining road, rail, coastal shipping, warehousing, cold chain and supply chain solutions on a unified platform rather than selling standalone transportation
- Deepen multimodal integration through a common technology backbone, unified governance framework and customer-centric visibility systems, so services are orchestrated as one ecosystem rather than offered independently
- Technology-led transformation: accelerate deployment of AI-enabled freight control towers, predictive analytics in Supply Chain Solutions, intelligent route optimisation to cut empty miles, automation and document digitisation, and advanced tracking across coastal shipping
- Expand global partnerships and trade connectivity to link domestic strength with international capability — exemplified by the collaboration with Flying Whales on next-generation logistics and future mobility
- Sustainability as a strategic imperative: shift volume toward rail and coastal to lower carbon intensity, expand alternative-fuel adoption across the fleet, build green/solar-powered warehousing and advance freight emissions measurement and reporting
- Invest in future-ready infrastructure — warehousing expansion in key consumption and manufacturing hubs, containerisation and multimodal infrastructure, technology integration and automation, EV-led transportation pilots, and international/regional logistics partnerships
- Maintain disciplined capital allocation focused on scalable capabilities, network efficiency and long-term competitiveness rather than scale alone
- Position as the logistics backbone for an export-driven, sustainable and digitally enabled India, aligned with Viksit Bharat 2047 and green corridors linked to emerging trade flows
- The Board has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, published on the Company's website, and dividends are recommended with reference to that policy; for FY26 the AGM notice puts a final dividend of Rs 1 per equity share of face value Rs 2 each to shareholders for declaration. The Company funds itself without public deposits — it has not accepted any deposit within the meaning of Sections 73 and 74 of the Companies Act during the year. Beyond distributions, the Company's stated intent is long-term value creation through sound governance: the Audit Committee scrutinises inter-corporate loans and investments, reviews utilisation of funds raised through issuances and statements of deviation, approves and monitors related party transactions, and considers schemes such as mergers, demergers and amalgamations. Social spend is channelled through its CSR arm, TCI Foundation, under a Board-approved CSR Policy.
- Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) framework across operations, with PPE provision, regular safety training and awareness programmes for drivers and employees, and stringent safety protocols for cargo handling and transportation
- 24x7 GPS-enabled fleet monitoring through centralised control towers to enhance road safety and operational oversight
- TCI Safe Safar initiative promoting health, safety and responsible driving practices among truck drivers and the broader transport community
- Employee welfare supported through medical and insurance coverage; retention supported through structured learning and development, upskilling/reskilling, leadership development, ESOPs and a robust grievance redressal mechanism
- Climate change formally identified as a material responsible-business-conduct risk in the BRSR, on the basis of disruption from extreme weather events such as cyclones, heat waves and floods
- Corporate governance, board oversight, ethics, risk management and compliance identified in the BRSR as a material issue with positive financial implications, backed by a Board-level governance framework, internal controls, compliance management and enterprise risk management processes
- Multimodal shift as the Company's stated decarbonisation lever — greater adoption of rail and coastal transportation to lower carbon intensity and improve fuel efficiency (MD&A/Chairman narrative; no quantified emissions target is disclosed in the routed sections)
- BRSR reporting boundary is standalone and no assurance was obtained (name and type of assurance provider both stated as 'Not Applicable'), so the sustainability disclosures are unassured and exclude subsidiaries
- Permanent-employee attrition disclosed at 8.73% total for FY 2025-26 (8.55% male, 13.65% female), improved from 9.88% in FY 2024-25; women represent 3.40% of total employees, 20% of the Board of Directors and 12.50% of KMPs
- CSR delivered through TCI Foundation in healthcare, education, sports, community development, skill development, employment generation and environment protection
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed sections carry no rupee capex plan, no named project with a commissioning date and no capacity-addition schedule; expansion is described qualitatively as footprint and capability build-out. The Chairman states that during the year the Company "continued to invest in strategic priorities including multimodal infrastructure, technology integra[tion]", while the Board's Report explicitly records that "there have been no material changes and commitments affecting the financial position of the Company between the end of the financial year and the date of this report". The existing asset footprint against which expansion is framed comprises 17 Mn. sq. ft. of warehousing space (dry and temperature controlled) with modern storage systems (RFID, ASRS, Pick/Put to Light), 67 yards managed across India, 4,500+ vehicles under operation of which 1,350+ are owned, and 180+ trains operated per month. Forward-looking capability expansion is stated at the divisional level for TCI Supply Chain Solutions: expansion of integrated 3PL and LLP service offerings, network optimisation and multimodal logistics capabilities, strategically located warehousing including temperature-controlled infrastructure, scalable storage solutions aligned with dynamic demand patterns, optimised network design for improved connectivity, and warehouse capacity gains via advanced design and vertical space optimization rather than footprint alone. The only capital-structure change disclosed for the year is the allotment of 135,035 equity shares on exercise of ESOP 2017 tranches 5, 6 and 7, taking the equity share count from 76,608,762 to 76,743,797 shares.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's economic formalisation is accelerating — GST collections rising and e-way bill volumes up 21% — translating directly into higher velocity and demand for integrated logistics
- Modal rebalancing: commissioning of 96.4% of Dedicated Freight Corridors is driving a decisive shift from road to rail, enhancing cost-efficiency for long-haul freight
- Structural shift from fragmented services to end-to-end, integrated, tech-enabled supply chains, with rising 4PL demand (~12% CAGR) reflecting a market-wide pivot to single-window outsourced logistics management
- Manufacturing integration: PLI schemes have catalysed over Rs 2.0 lakh crore of investment, requiring high-capacity multimodal logistics connecting factory zones to export hubs
- The EU–India FTA opening new export corridors in autos, pharma and advanced manufacturing, deepening India's integration with global value chains
- Climate-conscious trade rules and sustainability expectations making low-carbon, multimodal movement a necessity rather than an advantage
- Warehousing utilisation remained strong during the year, supported by manufacturing expansion and consumption-led demand; rail operations enhanced long-haul efficiency and network productivity; coastal shipping continued to scale with growing multimodal adoption
- Cold chain capabilities strengthened presence across pharmaceuticals, food and quick-commerce sectors
- Growth of e-commerce and quick commerce redefining warehousing strategy toward distributed networks, faster turnaround and efficient inventory positioning
- Digitalisation has moved from differentiator to baseline — ULIP has crossed 100 crore API transactions and India's logistics cost has reached ~7.97% of GDP — so operators without embedded technology operate at a structural disadvantage
- Sector consolidation and technology-led transformation, where TCI's scale, experience and execution capability are described as a competitive advantage
- Geopolitical volatility as a counterweight: the US-Israel and Iran conflict escalating since February 2026 has hit maritime choke points including the Strait of Hormuz, cut global air cargo capacity by approximately 18%, and spiked bunker fuel prices and war-risk surcharges

risks.note: Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications. Given operations in long-distance transportation, warehousing, cargo handling and movement of diverse consignments including hazardous and chemical goods, road accidents, driver fatigue, workplace incidents and health-related risks may adversely impact employees, business continuity, operational efficiency and stakeholder confidence. Mitigation is an EHS framework with PPE, driver and employee safety training, stringent cargo-handling protocols, 24x7 GPS-enabled fleet monitoring through centralised control towers, medical/insurance cover and the TCI Safe Safar driver initiative.
risks.risk: Occupational health and safety across long-haul transport, warehousing and hazardous-cargo handling

risks.note: Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: inability to attract, develop and retain skilled talent may impact operational efficiency, service quality, productivity and the Company's ability to meet customer expectations and growth objectives. Mitigated through structured learning and development, job rotation, upskilling/reskilling, leadership development, performance-based progression, recognition programmes, ESOPs and academic/industry partnerships for a talent pipeline.

Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications — worldwide businesses have reported newer and emerging cybersecurity threats such as ransomware, posing risk to everyday business operations. The Company states it has adequate cyber and IT security systems including ITDR, verified by external consultants with all recommendations implemented. Exposure is structurally rising as operations become dependent on proprietary TMS/WMS, control towers and digital documentation.

Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk: climate change can impact operations through extreme weather events such as cyclones, heat waves and floods, which have the potential to create severe disruptions to a pan-India road, rail and coastal network (the mitigation text is truncated in the routed source).
risks.risk: Climate change and extreme weather disruption

risks.note: The MD&A records that the US-Israel and Iran conflict, escalating since February 2026, has hit critical maritime choke points including the Strait of Hormuz, forcing vessel rerouting, suspended operations and a surge in war-risk surcharges and insurance premiums; Gulf airspace closures cut global air cargo capacity by approximately 18%; and energy-market volatility spiked bunker fuel prices, creating cascading cost pressure across supply chains. Coastal shipping and cross-border operations sit directly in this exposure.
risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption to trade lanes, energy and freight costs

risks.note: The BRSR workforce table shows Nil permanent workers against 8,904 workers who are 'other than permanent', alongside 4,165 permanent employees. Service quality, safety compliance and cost are therefore delivered largely through a non-permanent workforce and vendor/driver ecosystem the Company does not employ directly.
risks.risk: Structural dependence on a contract/outsourced workforce

risks.note: Exports contribute only 0.18% of total turnover and international presence is limited to three countries (Bangladesh, Nepal, UAE) with no international offices reported in the BRSR operations table, so earnings are tied almost entirely to Indian freight, warehousing and coastal demand cycles despite the Company's stated global-connectivity ambition.

The MD&A states that logistics digitalisation has shifted from a competitive advantage to a fundamental operational requirement and that organisations failing to embed technology into core workflows now operate at a structural disadvantage, with ~70% of logistics enterprises accelerating digital transformation — implying continuous, non-discretionary technology spend simply to hold position.
risks.risk: Competitive/technology displacement as digitalisation becomes the baseline

meta.thesis: TCIL is leveraging digital integration and strategic capacity expansion in high-margin segments like cold chain and coastal shipping to offset weak FTL/LTL freight demand, maintaining consistent top-line growth and net-debt-free balance sheet while building moats through end-to-end solutions for premium clients like Japanese FMCG firms.
